To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
court-appointed psychiatrists do not fulfil their role as critical experts in civil commitment hearings.
the APs’ contribution to court hearings was limited, and that their role was to a great extent built on therapeutic and collegial repertoires.

APs’ communication in civil commitment court proceedings is characterized by a therapeutic discourse that is built on the repertoire collegiality and that the therapeutic repertoire is built on the repertoires disclosing and mediating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what the function of APs should be in mental health law, and what is their contribution to the protection of the human rights of involuntarily committed patients.
the role and function of APs in mental health law and the potential for their role to be reformed.
the role of AP in civil commitment proceedings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the APs’ role is to support and not to challenge the recommendations from the treating psychiatrists, which is a role that is not compatible with their role as experts in the civil commitment process.
a medical model is not the best way to protect the rights of patients in civil commitment hearings.
the role of AP is not sufficiently clear and that this may be problematic for the human rights of the patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
APs are not fulfilling their role as independent experts.
the APs are not independent enough.
the role of AP should be to mediate the interests of the patient, the treating psychiatry and society at large, and to do this in a way that does not compromise the rights of patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of AP should not be therapeutic but instead be focused on protecting the legal rights of the patient.
the role of experts in mental health law needs to be reconsidered.
it is important to critically reflect upon the role of experts and to ensure that they are not just there for the sake of collegiality and therapy, but to ensure that patients’ rights are protected.
